questions.question: A person working on a disabled vehicle on the road shoulder:

options.text: Will likely pay attention to traffic.
May be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
Does not have to follow traffic laws.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be focused on repairs and not notice traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive carefully near people working on disabled vehicles. They are focused on their repair work and may not see traffic or other dangers nearby.

questions.question: After you finish a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Leave the rear shut-off valves open.
Leave the emergency line valve open.

questions.explanation: Before driving, open the rear emergency line and service line shut-off valves to check for air leaks. Close both valves before you start driving.

questions.question: What is the best way to check your lights during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Park near a mirror to see the reflection.
Turn on the lights, then get out to look at them.
Look at the dashboard warning lights.
Drive in traffic and wait for other drivers to signal you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on the lights, then get out to look at them.
questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, turn on your lights and then exit the vehicle to inspect them.

questions.question: How much liquid cargo you load should depend on:
questions.explanation: Consider liquid expansion during transport, the weight of the liquid, and legal weight limits. Be especially careful with dense liquids to stay within legal weight limits.

questions.question: Carrying liquid cargo:

options.text: Is easier than carrying solid cargo.
Is harder than carrying solid cargo.
Is not allowed during business hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is harder than carrying solid cargo.
questions.explanation: Transporting liquids in a tank requires special skill. Liquid surge creates dangers that make liquid cargo harder to haul than solid cargo.

questions.question: When backing a truck, you should:

options.text: Only use the driver's side mirror.
Only use the passenger's side mirror.

questions.explanation: Check both mirrors often when backing to watch for hazards. Use a helper to watch your blind spots whenever possible.

questions.question: Before backing under the trailer, make sure the trailer brakes are:
questions.explanation: When coupling trailers, follow the correct steps for safe operation. Lock the trailer brakes before backing your tractor under the trailer.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: When tailgated, create more space in front of your vehicle. This helps you avoid sudden stops that could cause a rear-end crash and makes it easier for the other driver to pass. Speeding up only makes things more dangerous.

questions.question: To prevent liquid surge in tanks, you should:
questions.explanation: Be aware of liquid surge when driving tank vehicles. Start, slow, and stop very smoothly to prevent surge problems.

questions.question: After a crash, basic procedures include all of these, except:
questions.explanation: After a crash, do three things: protect the area, notify authorities, and help injured people. Protect the accident site right away to prevent another crash from happening there.

questions.question: If you are not sure there is enough space for your vehicle under a bridge, you should:

options.text: Swerve as you pass under the bridge.

questions.explanation: Slow down if you are not sure your vehicle will fit under an overhead object. Find an alternate route if possible.

questions.question: You must put out emergency warning devices within ____ of stopping on the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Place emergency warning devices within 10 minutes of stopping on the road's shoulder. Turn on your four-way emergency flashers when you pull off the road.

questions.question: When stopped on the side of the road, a driver should:

options.text: Keep the driver's side door open.

questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. This is very important, especially at night.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver on the road, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay far away from a distracted driver. Be careful when passing because the driver may not see you and drift into your lane.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start driving. If your vehicle has a trailer, the trailer must be straight for accurate mirror adjustment.

questions.question: Looking far ahead while driving is:

options.text: Discouraged, as there is little you can do about something far up the road.
Encouraged to help you spot hazards early.
Only encouraged if you are transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encouraged to help you spot hazards early.
questions.explanation: Good drivers look 12 to 15 seconds ahead. This gives you time to see hazards and react safely.

questions.question: The correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tire with your hand.
Measuring the height of the tire.

questions.explanation: Check your tires before every trip and after every stop. Use a tire pressure gauge to check that tires are properly filled.

questions.question: If the road is covered in fog, the best choice is to:
questions.explanation: Driving in fog is dangerous. Do not drive if possible when fog is present.

questions.question: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers should:

options.text: Turn off once the vehicle begins moving.

questions.explanation: Warning lights and buzzers should turn off immediately after the engine starts. This includes the charging, oil, coolant, and ABS warning lights.

questions.question: When loading a tank, space must be left for outage. What is outage?

options.text: A place for luggage and personal items

questions.explanation: Liquids expand when heated. A tank must have extra empty space to allow liquids to expand safely.
